variants.title: The raccoon babies are coming down for dinner
variants.body: Mom goes first. The kits follow, one tiny paw at a time, and somebody always slips the last bit. (They're fine. Mostly embarrassed.)

variants.title: Raccoon family, now leaving the tree
variants.body: Mom, then a wobbly line of kits, just as it gets dark. They regroup at the bottom, sniff the air, and head out {place} like a very small parade.

variants.title: The raccoon kits are practicing climbing down
variants.body: Down is harder than up. Lots of hugging the trunk in the evening light. Mom waits at the bottom, not impressed, not worried.

variants.title: The raccoon kits are heading out for their first rounds
variants.body: Mom shimmies down the trunk as the streetlights flicker on and waits while the kits figure it out. Tonight's lesson: the quiet way along {street} toward {green}, where the snacks are.

variants.title: A raccoon is doing the nightly rounds
variants.body: Same route as last night: the can with the loose lid, then the one by the fence. Raccoons never forget a good lid.

variants.title: The night shift has clocked in
variants.body: Right now, somewhere {place}, a raccoon is patting along the curb with those clever little hands, reading the block by touch.

variants.title: A raccoon is investigating a very interesting lid
variants.body: Pry, wiggle, think, try again, in the dark. Raccoons are excellent at puzzles, especially the ones you didn't mean to set.

variants.title: A raccoon is walking the same route as always
variants.body: Down {street}, a careful pat along the curb, a peek behind {landmark}, then on toward {green}. They've done this loop so many nights they could do it with their eyes closed.

variants.title: A raccoon is splashing a snack around
variants.body: Rolling it between wet paws at a puddle tonight. They aren't washing it, exactly: wet paws just feel things better. Very fancy.

variants.title: Raccoon at the puddle, hands busy
variants.body: Dabble, dabble, squint, under the streetlight. Those front paws are so sensitive they're basically doing the looking.

variants.title: A raccoon found a puddle near {green}
variants.body: Sitting at the edge in the dark, rolling something between wet paws, totally absorbed. It looks like washing. It's really feeling.

variants.title: A raccoon is on a winter-prep snack tour
variants.body: Acorns, fallen apples, a dropped slice of pizza, all tonight. Fall is all-you-can-eat season, and they take it very seriously.

variants.title: Raccoon, getting extra fluffy for winter
variants.body: Every snack {place} tonight is going straight to the winter-coat fund. Chubby is the goal.

variants.title: A raccoon is on a serious fall snack mission
variants.body: Fallen apples, acorns, whatever the trees around {green} dropped today. They're out in the dark eating all of it, one bite at a time.

variants.title: A raccoon peeks out, then nopes back in
variants.body: It's getting dark, it's freezing, and one look outside was enough. The trash cans {place} can wait.

variants.title: The raccoons called in cozy
variants.body: The light is going and they're staying in, curled up in the den, tails over noses, waiting for a nicer night.

variants.title: The raccoons are sleeping in tonight
variants.body: Somewhere in a hollow tree near {green}, a raccoon family is piled into one warm, stripy heap. The cans on {street} will still be there when it's warmer.

variants.title: A raccoon mom is sneaking out for a quick bite
variants.body: As the light goes, she's slipping out of the den. The kits are tucked up high, and she'll be back before they wake.

variants.title: A raccoon mom just slipped out for a minute
variants.body: Her kits are tucked in a den high above {street}, too little to follow. She'll grab a quick bite near {green} before dark and hurry back.

variants.title: Raccoon mom, on a very short break
variants.body: Babies at home, snacks out here tonight. She moves fast, eats faster, and heads straight back to the pile.

variants.title: An opossum is tightrope-walking the fence
variants.body: Slow and steady in the dark, tail helping with the balance. Right now they're on bug and slug patrol {place}, in no rush at all.

variants.title: An opossum is out on a snack walk
variants.body: Fallen fruit, beetles, the odd snail, all tonight. They tidy up the block and ask for nothing in return. Model neighbor.

variants.title: A little white face is moving along the fence
variants.body: That's an opossum, waddling through under the streetlight. Pink nose, round ears, zero hurry.

variants.title: An opossum is taking the scenic route
variants.body: Along the fences behind {street} in the middle of the night, nose working the whole way. Slugs, fallen fruit, and absolutely no hurry.

variants.title: An opossum mom has passengers tonight
variants.body: A row of babies clings to her back, holding on tight while she waddles along in the dark. Best bus in town.

variants.title: Opossum mom, giving piggyback rides
variants.body: The babies are too big for her pouch now, so tonight they're riding on top instead. Nobody gets left behind.

variants.title: An opossum mom is giving the whole family a ride
variants.body: A row of tiny babies on her back as she waddles along the edge of {green}. One just slipped. She's waiting.

variants.title: A young opossum is out on their own for the first time
variants.body: It's just getting dark and everything is new: the curb, the hedge, the smell of the gardens {place}. They sniff all of it. Twice.

variants.title: A teenage opossum is exploring
variants.body: Fresh out of mom's care and very curious tonight. Every flowerpot needs a careful sniff.

variants.title: A young opossum is out exploring near {street}
variants.body: New to being on their own, giving every flowerpot a slow, curious sniff in the dark. Everything is interesting. Everything takes a while.

variants.title: The opossums are keeping their ears warm
variants.body: It's getting dark and cold, and bare ears and tails don't love winter. They're staying tucked in somewhere snug.

variants.title: Opossum, staying in under a pile of leaves
variants.body: Too chilly for a walk tonight. They'll pop out again on a milder night.

variants.title: The opossums are waiting out the cold
variants.body: Curled up somewhere snug near {green} tonight, under leaves or beneath a porch, pink nose tucked away.

variants.title: The moths are having a dance party at the streetlight
variants.body: Tonight they're looping around the lamp, steering by the brightest light above them. Every porch light switched off {place} helps them home.

variants.title: A little crowd is looping around the lamp
variants.body: Fuzzy wings, feathery antennae, dizzy loops in the dark. Some are as fancy as butterflies, just on the night shift.

variants.title: The moths found the streetlight again
variants.body: Round and round they go tonight. It's not a party they meant to join, and a dark porch lets them get back to their night.

variants.title: The moths have found the streetlight on {street}
variants.body: Dizzy and determined, steering by a light that isn't the moon. Every window that goes dark nearby helps one of them get back on course.

variants.title: The moths are covering the late shift at the flowers
variants.body: The bees are heading home and the moths are clocking in, sipping nectar and carrying pollen as it gets dark. Very underrated coworkers.

variants.title: A moth is sipping from a night flower
variants.body: Fuzzy, quiet and secretly doing important work in the dark. The garden {place} has a night crew.

variants.title: The night-shift pollinators are working {green}
variants.body: Bloom to bloom in the dark, sipping and carrying pollen. Most people never see them. The flowers know.

variants.title: The last moths of the year are fluttering by
variants.body: A mild fall evening, and a few are still out. Most are already tucked in the fallen leaves as cocoons.

variants.title: One brave fall moth is out tonight
variants.body: Everyone else is bundled up for winter. This one wanted one more evening.

variants.title: One of the year's last moths is out over {green}
variants.body: Unhurried in the mild dusk, one moth flutters by. Their friends are waiting for spring in the leaf litter.

variants.title: The pigeons are heading out for breakfast
variants.body: The streetlights just clicked off, and they're dropping off the ledge in little groups, landing {place} to see where last night's crumbs ended up.

variants.title: First flight of the morning
variants.body: A clap of wings, one loop around the block in the early light, and down they come. Breakfast is wherever the bagel crumbs are.

variants.title: The pigeons are doing their morning crumb inspection
variants.body: Strut, peck, strut. The block is still quiet, and every inch of sidewalk is getting a very official review before the crowds show up.

variants.title: The pigeons are heading out for breakfast on {street}
variants.body: Off the ledges in little flocks, one lap around {landmark}, then down to the same breakfast spots as yesterday. Same friends, same crumbs, early as ever.

variants.title: A pigeon is sunbathing like it's vacation
variants.body: Flat on a warm ledge in the middle of the day, one wing tipped up, eyes half closed. They'll stay like this until the shade comes around.

variants.title: A pigeon is lying flat on a warm ledge
variants.body: Feathers fluffed, wing out, fully melted. The busy block is going on below. Do not disturb.

variants.title: A pigeon is soaking up the sun near {landmark}
variants.body: Wing tipped open, eyes half shut, pressed flat to the warm stone. Right now that's the whole plan for the day, and it's going great.

variants.title: A pigeon is showing off his best moves
variants.body: The morning has barely started and he's already puffed up, turning round and round and bowing on the sidewalk, cooing the whole time. She keeps eating like she hasn't noticed. She noticed.

variants.title: Pigeon romance is happening on {street}
variants.body: First thing this morning: neck puffed and shimmering, a spin, a bow, a coo. She's pretending breakfast is more interesting. He'll be back at it in a minute.

variants.title: Pigeon romance is happening on the sidewalk
variants.body: Puff, spin, bow, coo, right in the middle of everyone's day. People step around him. He doesn't care. She's watching, a little.

variants.title: A pigeon is courting along {street}
variants.body: His neck is shining green and purple, and he's turning round and round her between the busy feet. She takes two steps away. He follows, still cooing.

variants.title: A pigeon is carrying one extremely important twig
variants.body: Up from the curb, across the block, and onto a ledge {place}. Somewhere up there a nest is coming together, one twig at a time, in the middle of the day.

variants.title: Pigeon, busy with home improvements
variants.body: Another twig, another trip. The nest is famously minimal and they like it that way. One more and maybe they'll call it a day.

variants.title: A pigeon is flying one perfect twig home
variants.body: Over {street} and up to a ledge a few floors above everyone's heads. Their partner is waiting to tuck it in place.

variants.title: The pigeons are wearing their puffy coats
variants.body: The morning is chilly, so they're fluffed into little down jackets, pressed together on the ledge, waiting for the first light to reach the stone.

variants.title: The pigeons are huddled on the bright side of {landmark}
variants.body: Shoulder to shoulder in the early light, puffed up like gray pillows, nobody moving until the ledge warms up.

variants.title: Pigeon huddle in progress
variants.body: Shoulder to shoulder on the warm side of the ledge in the middle of the day. Every time the sun slides, the whole row shuffles to follow it.

variants.title: The pigeons are puffed up on a ledge along {street}
variants.body: A tight gray row in the daytime warmth, eyes half closed. Every few minutes someone wiggles in a little closer.

variants.title: The pigeons are back on the ledge
variants.body: The light is going and pairs are settling in side by side, the same ledge and the same partner as last night.

variants.title: Pigeon bedtime is starting
variants.body: As the streetlights flicker on, they flap up one by one to the ledge {place} and shuffle in next to their favorite pigeon.

variants.title: The pigeons are coming home to their ledge
variants.body: Pairs are flapping up above {street} as it gets dark, settling in side by side with a few sleepy coos. Same spot as every evening.

variants.title: The pigeons are asleep on the ledge
variants.body: Heads tucked into their back feathers, pressed together in pairs a few floors above the sidewalk {place}. They'll be up at first light, hungry.

variants.title: A pigeon is dozing on one foot
variants.body: Feathers fluffed, head tucked, the other foot pulled up into the warm. Late buses go by underneath. Not one bit bothered.

variants.title: The pigeons are asleep above {street}
variants.body: Tucked into the ledges in pairs while the block hums along below. Nobody stirs until morning.

variants.title: A pigeon is bobbing down the sidewalk
variants.body: Bob, step, bob, step through the early quiet. Every bob holds their view perfectly still, which is very handy when you're looking for breakfast crumbs.

variants.title: A pigeon is strutting along {street}
variants.body: First pigeon on the block this morning, head going like a little metronome. Very serious. Very silly. Very focused on that muffin crumb.

variants.title: Pigeon, on patrol
variants.body: Head forward, freeze, body catches up. They're working the whole block in the middle of the day, between everyone's shoes.

variants.title: A pigeon is bobbing past the café tables on {street}
variants.body: Bob, step, bob, step. Every bob keeps the view steady, like a camera on a gimbal, and right now the view is all crumbs.

variants.title: A pigeon is sipping from a puddle
variants.body: Beak in, one long slurp, no head tipping. They're taking a midday drink like they're using a straw.

variants.title: A pigeon is drinking near {green}
variants.body: Beak down in the puddle, a long steady sip in the middle of the day. Most birds tip their heads back to swallow. Not this one.

variants.title: A pigeon found the good puddle
variants.body: One long pull of water, then a quick look around, then another. The other birds are doing it the hard way.

variants.title: Two pigeons are preening each other
variants.body: Good morning, pigeon style: gently nibbling the feathers on each other's necks, the spots they can't reach themselves. Then breakfast.

variants.title: A pigeon couple is getting cozy near {landmark}
variants.body: Side by side in the early light, taking turns fixing each other's neck feathers before the day gets going.

variants.title: A pigeon is getting a neck rub
variants.body: The light is going and their partner is tidying the feathers they can't reach. Eyes half closed. Total bliss before bed.

variants.title: Two pigeons are preening on a ledge along {street}
variants.body: End of the day, side by side, nibbling each other's necks while the streetlights come on below.

variants.title: A pigeon just took off with a CLAP
variants.body: Early-morning show-off: he snaps his wings together on takeoff, then glides with them held up in a V. Very dramatic for this hour.

variants.title: A pigeon is showing off over {street}
variants.body: Clap, clap, then a long gliding swoop overhead, wings raised high. It's for the pigeon he likes. She's pretending not to watch.

variants.title: Pigeon air show
variants.body: A few loud wing claps overhead, then a slow, swooping glide. Somebody's trying to impress somebody in the middle of the day.

variants.title: A pigeon is flying food home to the nest
variants.body: Up to a ledge {place} and behind the air conditioner. The squabs back there are getting a midday meal of crop milk, straight from mom or dad.

variants.title: A pigeon is heading home with food near {landmark}
variants.body: Somewhere up on a ledge, squabs are waiting with their mouths open. The babies stay hidden until they're almost grown, so you'll only ever see the parents coming and going.

variants.title: A pigeon just slipped behind an air conditioner
variants.body: There's a nest back there, and one or two squabs getting their midday feeding. Give it a few weeks and they'll be out on the sidewalk too.

variants.title: The pigeons are wheeling over the rooftops
variants.body: The whole flock turns at once in the middle of the day, flashing their pale underwings. One spooks, everyone goes.

variants.title: A flock of pigeons is circling over {street}
variants.body: Up, around, back down to the same ledge. Nobody knows who decided. It looks great anyway.

variants.title: Pigeon flock, all at once
variants.body: They lift off together, loop overhead in a tight swirl and land almost exactly where they started. Then they do it again.

variants.title: A pigeon has puffed up into a ball
variants.body: It's getting dark and cold, so they've fluffed into a round gray ball and sat right down on their feet to keep their toes warm.

variants.title: Pigeons are huddling on a ledge near {landmark}
variants.body: The light is going and they're pressed together out of the wind, feathers puffed, toes tucked. Round, gray and cozy for the night.

variants.title: A pigeon is wearing their winter puffer
variants.body: Twice their usual size tonight, toes tucked, and very proud of it.

variants.title: The pigeons are huddled tight on a cold ledge along {street}
variants.body: Pressed together in the dark, puffed up and still. Sharing the warmth until morning.

variants.title: A pigeon is asleep on their home ledge
variants.body: The same ledge as last night, and the night before. Tonight they're tucked in right where they always come back to.

variants.title: The pigeons are home for the night near {landmark}
variants.body: Heads tucked, pairs side by side, the same spot as always. Pigeons are champion homebodies.

variants.title: A pigeon is tucked in on the ledge they always come back to
variants.body: Racing pigeons can find home from hundreds of miles away. Tonight, this one only had to find this exact ledge, and did.

variants.title: The sparrow gang is up and talking
variants.body: It's barely light and the hedge {place} is already chattering. That racket is how they check who made it through the night. Also gossip, probably.

variants.title: Good morning from the hedge
variants.body: Cheep, cheep, CHEEP. The sun isn't even all the way up and the sparrows already have opinions about the day.

variants.title: The sparrow gang is waking up the block
variants.body: The hedges along {street} just switched on: who's here, who found breakfast, who's being dramatic. In a minute they'll all pour out onto the sidewalk.

variants.title: The sparrows are taking a dust bath
variants.body: A dry patch of dirt by the curb, three sparrows wriggling in it at once, wings flicking dust everywhere. Dry shampoo, sparrow style, in the middle of the day.

variants.title: Sparrow spa day at the curb
variants.body: Wiggle, flap, fluff, repeat. Right now they're scrubbing out oil and tiny bugs, and somehow coming out cleaner.

variants.title: The sparrows are having a dust bath near {green}
variants.body: Belly down in a dusty hollow, flapping like they're swimming in it. Everyone's waiting their turn for the good spot, mostly patiently.

variants.title: Sparrow kids are begging very dramatically
variants.body: The morning has barely started and the fluffy youngsters are already chasing their parents, wings fluttering, beaks wide open. The parents mostly give in.

variants.title: Baby sparrows are begging all over {street}
variants.body: First thing this morning, curb to hedge to curb, mouths open, wings shaking. The grown-ups look tired already. They keep feeding them anyway.

variants.title: A baby sparrow is following a grown-up everywhere
variants.body: Flutter, flutter, CHEEP, in the middle of the busy sidewalk. The grown-up finds a bug, and the baby finds a way to be standing right there.

variants.title: Sparrow kids are begging under the café tables on {street}
variants.body: Two fluffy youngsters, one tired parent, and a dropped croissant. Everyone is yelling. Rush hour, sparrow style.

variants.title: A sparrow is stuffing grass into a gap
variants.body: A sign, a traffic light, a hole in old brick: right now they're cramming in grass for a messy, cozy nest. Interior design: maximal.

variants.title: Sparrow construction season is open
variants.body: Bits of grass, feathers and string are going into every nook {place} today. The result is lumpy and perfect.

variants.title: A sparrow is moving into a gap near {landmark}
variants.body: Back and forth with beakfuls of grass and the odd bit of string, all day if it takes that long. It won't win any design awards. It will be very cozy.

variants.title: The hedge is having its evening meeting
variants.body: As the light goes, the whole gang piles into the bushes and talks over the day. Loudly. Everyone has a point.

variants.title: The sparrows are arguing about bedtime
variants.body: Lots of chirping and shuffling in the hedge as it gets dark, then suddenly, quiet. They've settled it.

variants.title: The hedge on {street} is having its evening meeting
variants.body: Every sparrow on the block is in there right now, chattering about the day before bed. Any minute it'll go quiet all at once. Meeting adjourned.

variants.title: The sparrows are tiny fluffballs today
variants.body: Puffed up round, shoulder to shoulder, deep in the hedge and out of the wind. Every so often one pops out for a seed and zips right back.

variants.title: The sparrows are huddled deep in the hedge
variants.body: Puffed into round little balls, packed shoulder to shoulder out of the wind along {street}. Small birds, big huddle, warm enough for now.

variants.title: Sparrow sleepover in the hedge
variants.body: It's getting dark and cold, so everyone's packing in close for the night. Small birds, big huddle.

variants.title: The sparrows are crowding into the hedge on {street}
variants.body: The light is going, the air is cold, and they're squeezing into the middle of the bush, fluffing up for a long winter night.

variants.title: The sparrow gang is asleep in the hedge
variants.body: Deep inside the bushes tonight, all puffed up together. The chatter starts again at first light. Count on it.

variants.title: Lights out in the hedge
variants.body: For a few hours, the loudest bushes {place} are completely quiet.

variants.title: Lights out in the sparrow hedge
variants.body: Deep in the bushes along {street}, the whole gang is asleep, feathers fluffed. The loudest hedge in the neighborhood is quiet until morning.

variants.title: A squirrel is hiding an acorn
variants.body: Dig, drop, pat-pat-pat, then a very suspicious look around in the morning quiet. You saw nothing.

variants.title: A squirrel is planting an acorn in {green}
variants.body: First job of the morning: dig, drop, pat-pat-pat, and a quick look to see who's watching. The ones they forget might be oak trees someday.

variants.title: Squirrels are filling every planter on the block
variants.body: Today every planter {place} is a pantry. They'll find lots of these again by memory. The rest might sprout in spring. Oops, a forest.

variants.title: A squirrel is pretending to bury something
variants.body: Someone's watching, so they're faking it: dig, pat, nothing there. The real snack is about to go somewhere secret.

variants.title: The squirrels are up and digging
variants.body: Morning is rush hour. Right now they're checking old hiding spots and sniffing out breakfast {place}.

variants.title: A squirrel is speed-running the lawn
variants.body: Dash, stop, sniff, dig, dash. The day is just starting and they have a lot of places to check.

variants.title: The squirrels are making their morning rounds
variants.body: Up and down the trees on {street}, checking old hiding spots, sniffing for breakfast. Morning is their busiest time.

variants.title: Two squirrels are chasing each other around the tree
variants.body: Wild spirals up and down the trunk in the middle of the day. It's courting season, and nobody is being subtle about it.

variants.title: Squirrel loop-de-loops on the tree trunk
variants.body: Round and round and round, right now, for no reason anyone else can see. In winter, these chases are mostly about romance. Very dizzy romance.

variants.title: Two squirrels are chasing around a tree near {green}
variants.body: Up, down and around the trunk so fast it's dizzying. They'll stop, glare at each other, and start again.

variants.title: A squirrel is splooting
variants.body: Flat on a cool branch in the hottest part of the day, belly down, legs out like a little rug. That's how a squirrel beats the heat.

variants.title: Squirrel pancake on the branch
variants.body: Too hot to scamper. They've spread out flat in the shade and they are not getting up until it cools off.

variants.title: A squirrel is lying flat as a pancake
variants.body: Stretched belly-down on a cool branch over {street}, legs out, done with today's heat. The most relatable thing in nature.

variants.title: A squirrel mom is heading home to the drey
variants.body: Her babies are tucked up in that ball of leaves, and she's checking on them between midday snack runs.

variants.title: A squirrel mom is checking on her babies
variants.body: Up the trunk to a ball of leaves high above {green}. Her kits are tucked inside. A quick peek, then back out for more snacks.

variants.title: Busy mom, coming through
variants.body: The light is going. Up the trunk to the leafy nest, one last check on the kits, and in for the night.

variants.title: A squirrel is heading up for the night
variants.body: The light is going, so it's up the trunk to the drey, tail flicking. Bedtime comes early for squirrels.

variants.title: Last snack, then bed
variants.body: One final nibble as it gets dark, then straight up the tree. Squirrels keep very responsible hours.

variants.title: A squirrel is climbing home near {green}
variants.body: One last snack, then up the tree to the leafy drey before dark. Lights out early.

variants.title: A squirrel is curled up in the drey
variants.body: Wrapped in their own tail like a blanket, high in a ball of leaves tonight. On cold nights, sometimes two share.

variants.title: Squirrel, fast asleep in a leaf ball
variants.body: That messy clump of leaves up in the tree {place}? Tonight there's a very cozy squirrel inside.

variants.title: A squirrel is fast asleep in the drey
variants.body: High in a tree near {green}, curled inside a ball of leaves, tail wrapped around like a blanket until morning.

variants.title: The starlings are lining up on the wire
variants.body: Dozens of them as the light goes, chattering and swapping places, about to head off together to a shared roost for the night.

variants.title: A starling is doing impressions
variants.body: Listen: a whistle, a click, maybe a car alarm. Right now a starling on the wire {place} is remixing the whole block into one evening song.

variants.title: Starling group chat, live on the wire
variants.body: So much chatter as it gets dark. Then, all at once, everybody takes off. Meeting adjourned.

variants.title: The starlings are gathering on the wires over {street}
variants.body: Dozens of them in the evening light, chattering and shuffling down the wire. Any second now they'll all lift off toward their night roost.

variants.title: Starlings are poking holes in the lawn
variants.body: Stab, open, snack. Right now they're pushing their beaks into the grass and popping them open to pry up grubs.

variants.title: The starlings are lawn-aerating for free
variants.body: A shiny little work crew marching across the grass in the middle of the day: poke, open, snack, keep moving.

variants.title: The starlings are working the grass at {green}
variants.body: Beaks in, beaks open, grubs out. They're marching across the lawn in a loose line, glinting purple and green.

variants.title: A starling is putting on a rooftop concert
variants.body: The morning has barely started and they're up on the roof in glossy purple and green, wings flicking, singing every sound they know.

variants.title: A starling is singing from a chimney
variants.body: Whistles, clicks, a borrowed car alarm, first thing this morning. Spring starlings are very committed performers.

variants.title: A starling is singing from a chimney above {street}
variants.body: Wings flicking in the early light, mixing whistles and clicks and maybe somebody's ringtone into one long spring song. Whole heart in it.

variants.title: Young starlings are following their parents around
variants.body: Plain brown and very loud this morning, trailing the grown-ups across the grass and begging for breakfast bugs.

variants.title: Starling teens are being extremely loud
variants.body: They look nothing like the shiny grown-ups yet, but the early-morning volume is already perfect.

variants.title: Young starlings are following their parents across {green}
variants.body: Brown, fluffy and yelling, right behind the shiny grown-ups. Every time a parent finds a grub, three beaks open.

variants.title: The starlings are wearing their stars
variants.body: Lined up on the wire in the middle of the day, covered in white winter speckles. When the light catches them, they sparkle.

variants.title: Starling, polka dots edition
variants.body: Dark and spotted all over right now, like a little starry sky with legs, chattering on the wire.

variants.title: The starlings are sparkling on a wire over {street}
variants.body: Covered in tiny white speckles and fluffed against the cold. When the light hits just right, they look like little starry skies.

variants.title: A mourning dove is cooing
variants.body: Hoo-OO-oo-oo, soft and slow from a wire {place} in the early light. It isn't sad at all. It's a love song.

variants.title: A mourning dove is going hoo-OO-oo-oo
variants.body: It sounds a bit gloomy for this early in the morning, but that's actually flirting.

variants.title: A mourning dove is cooing softly on {street}
variants.body: Hoo-OO-oo-oo, from a wire somewhere above, first thing this morning. Someone nearby is listening.

variants.title: Two doves are sitting very close
variants.body: Side by side on the wire in the middle of the day, preening each other. Adorable, honestly.

variants.title: A dove couple is sharing the wire
variants.body: A little nudge, a little preen, a long nap in between. They're doing their best impression of a valentine.

variants.title: Two mourning doves are sitting close together
variants.body: Side by side on a wire near {green}, gently preening each other while the day goes by underneath.

variants.title: A dove is building the world's simplest nest
variants.body: A few twigs on a fire escape. Today, somehow, that's enough. Minimalism wins again.

variants.title: Mourning dove, nest-building on a budget
variants.body: Twig, twig, done. Right now they're settling onto a nest so thin you can almost see through it.

variants.title: A dove is building a tiny nest near {landmark}
variants.body: A few twigs balanced on a fire escape, carried up one at a time all day. In a couple of weeks there might be chicks.

variants.title: Mourning doves are picking at seeds
variants.body: A small group is walking the ground in the early light, bobbing their heads. If something startles them, listen for the whistle of their wings.

variants.title: Mourning doves are strolling through {green}
variants.body: Breakfast stroll: a little group walking slowly, bobbing and picking up seeds while the grass is still wet.

variants.title: Head-bob parade on the ground
variants.body: The doves are strolling and snacking in the middle of the day. Spook them and their wings squeak like a toy.

variants.title: The doves are soaking up the last sun
variants.body: Puffed up on the wire, facing the sunset, catching every bit of warmth before night.

variants.title: Dove, fluffed up to maximum
variants.body: Round as a dinner roll, eyes half closed, enjoying the last warm light {place}.

variants.title: The doves are catching the last warm light
variants.body: Puffed up round on a wire over {street}, facing the sunset, soaking up every bit of warmth before dark.

variants.title: A robin is kicking off the dawn chorus
variants.body: The sun isn't up yet, and one robin is singing. Then another. Listen for a cheery, rolling song {place}.

variants.title: The robins are up before everyone
variants.body: It's still mostly dark, and they're already singing like it's the best morning ever.

variants.title: A robin is singing the neighborhood awake
variants.body: It's barely light, and a robin near {green} is already singing. Another answers from down {street}. The dawn chorus has begun.

variants.title: A robin is hunting worms
variants.body: The grass is still wet this morning: run, stop, tilt the head, pounce. That tilt isn't listening. They're looking with one eye.

variants.title: A robin is hunting worms in {green}
variants.body: Breakfast run across the dewy lawn: run, stop, tilt, and a sudden stab at the tiniest wiggle.

variants.title: Robin vs. worm, round one
variants.body: A tug, a stretch, a tug, right there in the middle of the lawn. The robin usually wins. The worm is putting up a good fight.

variants.title: A robin fledgling is figuring things out
variants.body: Spotty chest, stubby tail, lots of hopping. A parent is a few feet away with a worm right now. No rescue needed.

variants.title: Baby robin, hopping around like a wind-up toy
variants.body: Not flying well yet, but mom and dad are watching from the fence. Give them space and they'll be fine.

variants.title: A baby robin is hopping around {green}
variants.body: Spotty chest, stubby tail, not quite flying. A parent just landed with a worm. This little one is right where they're supposed to be.

variants.title: The robins are raiding the berry bushes
variants.body: Worms are getting scarce, so right now it's fruit: a whole group gulping down a berry tree in the middle of the day.

variants.title: Robin berry buffet is open
variants.body: Gulp, gulp, gulp. They're in full fruit mode today, passing berries down the branch.

variants.title: The robins are feasting on berries near {green}
variants.body: A flock is working through a berry tree, gulping happily. By the end of the day it'll be bare.

variants.title: A robin is singing the day out
variants.body: First to sing this morning and still going as the light fades. Long shift. Great attitude.

variants.title: One more song from the robin
variants.body: As it gets dark {place}, a robin is still singing, cheerful as ever.

variants.title: A robin is singing the day out
variants.body: The light is fading over {street} and one robin is still going from a high branch. First voice in the morning, one of the last at night.

variants.title: A quiet flock of robins is passing through
variants.body: Plenty of robins stay all winter. This morning they're moving through the trees together, quiet, looking for berries.

variants.title: Surprise, the robins never left
variants.body: A little flock just landed in the bare branches this morning. In winter they stop singing, so you might not notice them. They're here.

variants.title: A quiet flock of robins is passing through {green}
variants.body: Early this morning, a dozen robins in the treetops, not singing, just looking for breakfast berries. Still your neighbors.

variants.title: The robins are at a big sleepover
variants.body: Tonight dads and young robins are sleeping together in one big group roost. At dawn they'll scatter.

variants.title: Robins, roosting in the trees
variants.body: Dozens of them tucked into the branches tonight, resting up for tomorrow's very early concert.

variants.title: The robins are at their big sleepover
variants.body: Dozens tucked into the trees near {green}, sleeping together in one group roost. At first light they'll head back to their own patches.

variants.title: A gull is riding the wind
variants.body: Wings barely moving, drifting over the rooftops {place} in the middle of the day like it's no effort at all. It mostly isn't.

variants.title: A gull is just hanging in the air
variants.body: No flapping, no hurry. Right now they've found the perfect breeze and they're keeping it.

variants.title: A gull is gliding over {water}
variants.body: Wings out, barely moving, riding the breeze off the water. Every so often they tilt, just a little, and drift off down the shore.

variants.title: A gull is cracking a clam the clever way
variants.body: Up, up, then drop it on the rocks. It didn't break. Up again. They'll be at this for a while.

variants.title: Gull vs. clam
variants.body: The gull has a plan: fly high, let go, check the result. Repeat until it pops open.

variants.title: A gull is cracking a clam on the rocks by {water}
variants.body: Up high, drop, check. Not yet? Up again. Right now the whole beach is watching to see who gets it first.

variants.title: A gull has claimed a piling
variants.body: Standing very tall in the early light, watching the water {place} to see what the morning tide brings in. That piling is taken.

variants.title: Gull, on morning lookout
variants.body: Up on a post at first light, judging the harbor. Breakfast could show up any minute.

variants.title: A gull is keeping watch from a post on {water}
variants.body: Feathers ruffling in the morning breeze, staring down the tide. That post is theirs, and everyone knows it.

variants.title: The gulls are heading out to the water for the night
variants.body: As the sky goes pink, they're flying out over the harbor to sleep floating together, safe from anything on land.

variants.title: Gull commute, outbound
variants.body: The light is going and the gulls are streaming out over the water to their floating bedroom.

variants.title: The gulls are flying out to {water} for the night
variants.body: Long loose lines of them in the evening sky, headed out to sleep on the waves.

variants.title: A gull is guarding a rooftop nest
variants.body: Up on a flat roof in the middle of the day, standing over a nest. Get too close and you'll hear about it. Loudly.

variants.title: Gull parent on roof duty
variants.body: Somewhere up there is a nest, and right now the gull standing guard is taking the job very seriously.

variants.title: A gull is guarding a nest on a rooftop near {street}
variants.body: Chest out, staring down a passing crow. Their partner will take the next shift.

variants.title: A young gull is whining for food
variants.body: Mottled brown, as big as the grown-ups, and begging right now. The red spot on a parent's beak is the doorbell.

variants.title: Gull teenager, still asking parents for snacks
variants.body: Full-size, fully capable, extremely whiny, following a parent down the beach in the middle of the day.

variants.title: A young gull is whining by {water}
variants.body: Mottled brown, already grown-up size, ringing the red-spot doorbell on a parent's beak over and over.

variants.title: Shh, the gulls are finally asleep
variants.body: All tucked in together on the harbor tonight, bobbing like bath toys. For once, nobody is yelling.

variants.title: The gulls are asleep on the water
variants.body: Floating out on the harbor in the dark, rising and falling with the waves.

variants.title: The gulls are asleep out on {water}
variants.body: Floating together, tucked in, bobbing on the night water. The loudest birds in the neighborhood are quiet until morning.

variants.title: A monarch is drinking from the flowers
variants.body: Wings opening and closing slowly in the middle of the day. Every sip is fuel for a very big trip.

variants.title: Monarch at the snack bar
variants.body: Flower to flower, sip, sip, right now. That bright orange is a warning to birds: they taste terrible.

variants.title: A monarch is drinking from the flowers in {green}
variants.body: Moving bloom to bloom, wings opening and closing. This one is fueling up for a long trip, and taking it seriously.

variants.title: A monarch is flying to Mexico
variants.body: Drifting over the rooftops right now, headed for mountains they've never seen. Today's stop: a snack break {place}. No map needed.

variants.title: Tiny traveler, passing through
variants.body: A monarch is flying south over the block in the middle of the day. Thousands of miles to go, one flap at a time.

variants.title: A monarch is passing through {green} on the way to Mexico
variants.body: Down for a quick rest and a sip, then up and south again. They know the way.

variants.title: A monarch is laying eggs on milkweed
variants.body: One tiny egg per leaf, right now, in the middle of the day. Milkweed is the only plant her caterpillars can eat.

variants.title: Monarch mom, very particular about milkweed
variants.body: She's tasting each leaf with her feet before leaving an egg. Only the best for the kids.

variants.title: A monarch is leaving eggs on milkweed near {green}
variants.body: Land, taste with her feet, one tiny egg, move on. She'll do this all day.

variants.title: The monarchs are settling in for the night
variants.body: As the light goes, travelers are folding their wings together on one branch, resting before tomorrow's leg of the trip.

variants.title: Monarch hotel, now open
variants.body: A few butterflies are bunking on the same branch {place} tonight. Big day of flying tomorrow.

variants.title: Monarchs are resting together near {green}
variants.body: A cluster of orange folding up on a branch as it gets dark. Tomorrow they keep flying south.

variants.title: A red-tailed hawk is sitting very, very still
variants.body: Up on a ledge {place} in the middle of the day, watching the ground below. They've been there an hour already, waiting for one good chance.

variants.title: Hawk on a light pole, doing nothing on purpose
variants.body: It looks like a nap. It is not a nap. Right now they're watching everything that moves.

variants.title: A red-tailed hawk is watching over {street}
variants.body: Up on {landmark}, perfectly still, eyes on the ground. Every pigeon on the block has noticed. Nobody's moving.

variants.title: A hawk is circling overhead
variants.body: Wide, lazy loops on the rising warm air of the day. Look up for the rusty red tail when they bank.

variants.title: Free elevator ride for the hawk
variants.body: Right now they're riding warm air up and up without a single flap. Effortless, and a little show-offy.

variants.title: A hawk is circling high above {green}
variants.body: Slow loops, hardly a flap, getting smaller as they rise. When they bank, the red tail glows.

variants.title: Two red-tails are on a sky date
variants.body: Soaring together in big circles right now. Sometimes one dives and they touch talons in the air. Very dramatic.

variants.title: Red-tailed hawk romance, overhead
variants.body: Matching loops, a swoop, a near miss on purpose, all in the middle of the day. Winter is courting season.

variants.title: Two red-tailed hawks are dancing in the sky
variants.body: Soaring together above {green} in matching circles. Any second now one will dive toward the other.

variants.title: A red-tail is sitting on eggs
variants.body: Hunkered down on a big stick nest in the early light, keeping the eggs warm while the city wakes up. Their partner is out hunting breakfast.

variants.title: A red-tail is keeping eggs warm near {landmark}
variants.body: First light on a nest of sticks high on a ledge, and a hawk sitting very still on it. Good morning, very patient parent.

variants.title: Hawk, on nest duty
variants.body: Hunkered down on a giant pile of sticks in the middle of the day, keeping the eggs warm while the city goes by underneath.

variants.title: A young hawk is screaming for breakfast
variants.body: That long wheeze at first light is a fledgling asking the parents to hurry up. They can fly now. Hunting is still a work in progress.

variants.title: Hawk teen, very loud, very hungry
variants.body: Flying fine, hunting badly, so they're yelling from the tree in the middle of the day. A lot.

variants.title: A young hawk is calling over {green}
variants.body: That long, wheezy scream from the treetops is a fledgling asking a parent to bring something, anything, right now.

variants.title: A hawk is tucking in for the night
variants.body: As the light goes, they're perched close to a tree trunk, out of the wind, done for the day.

variants.title: Hawk, off the clock
variants.body: Shift's over. Feathers fluffed, tucked against the trunk, eyes closing as it gets dark.

variants.title: A hawk is settling in for the night
variants.body: Perched close against a tree trunk near {green}, feathers fluffed. Tomorrow morning, the watch begins again.

variants.title: A blue jay is stuffing acorns in their throat
variants.body: Up early at the oak tree, cramming several into a stretchy throat pouch at once. The ones they forget will grow into oaks {place}.

variants.title: A blue jay is planting oaks around {green}
variants.body: First job of the morning: grab acorns, fly off, bury them all over. This jay is quietly growing a forest.

variants.title: Blue jay, burying treasure
variants.body: Acorn here, acorn there, all day long. Jays plant more oak trees than most people ever will.

variants.title: A blue jay is pretending to be a hawk
variants.body: That scream from the trees right now might be a jay. Maybe it clears everyone off the good branch. Maybe it's just fun.

variants.title: That hawk scream is really a blue jay
variants.body: Nope, no hawk. That's a blue jay doing their best impression in the middle of the day. They're very good at it.

variants.title: A blue jay is doing their best hawk impression
variants.body: That scream from the trees near {green}? Probably a jay. Look at the bird feeder: everyone just left.

variants.title: A blue jay is announcing the morning
variants.body: JAY! JAY! Bright blue against bare branches in the early light, and very loud about it.

variants.title: A blue jay is shouting good morning
variants.body: No alarm clock needed {place} today. The jays have it covered.

variants.title: A blue jay is announcing the morning from a branch over {street}
variants.body: Bright blue, very loud, absolutely sure everyone should be awake by now.

variants.title: A blue jay is being suspiciously quiet
variants.body: Right now the loudest bird on the block is slipping in and out of the leaves without a sound. There's a nest nearby.

variants.title: Blue jay in stealth mode
variants.body: Usually the loudest bird around. Today, sneaky as a spy, with a beakful of something for the nest.

variants.title: A blue jay is sneaking through the trees near {green}
variants.body: Not one jay! all day. That means a nest, and they're keeping it secret.

variants.title: A blue jay family is on a field trip
variants.body: First thing this morning, the youngsters are following the grown-ups through the trees and copying everything they do.

variants.title: Young blue jays are learning the ropes
variants.body: Watch a grown-up, try it, mess it up, try again, in the middle of the day. Very relatable.

variants.title: A blue jay family is on a field trip through {green}
variants.body: Tree to tree, the kids right behind, yelling whenever a grown-up finds a snack.

variants.title: Juncos are hopping under the hedge
variants.body: Little gray birds with snowy bellies, scratching for breakfast seeds in the morning chill. When they fly, their tails flash white.

variants.title: Juncos are hopping under the hedges on {street}
variants.body: First light, frosty leaves, and a little flock kicking through them for seeds. They don't walk. They hop.

variants.title: Tiny snowbirds, hop-hop-hopping
variants.body: Under every bush {place} in the middle of the day, a junco or two, hopping and scratching.

variants.title: The first juncos just landed
variants.body: They flew down from Canada overnight and touched down {place} this morning. They'll stay till spring.

variants.title: The snowbirds are back
variants.body: The first chilly morning, and here they are, hopping under the hedge. Welcome back, little gray friends.

variants.title: The juncos just arrived from Canada
variants.body: They flew all night and landed near {green} at first light. Right now they're already hopping under the hedges like they never left.

variants.title: A junco is trilling before the trip north
variants.body: A quick, bright trill from a branch in the early light. In a few weeks they'll be gone till fall.

variants.title: Junco, warming up for the road
variants.body: A morning trill, a lot of snacking. Canada is a long way to fly.

variants.title: A junco is trilling from a branch near {green}
variants.body: Bright little songs this morning, practicing for the trip north.

variants.title: The juncos are tucking into the hedge for the night
variants.body: As the light goes, a small flock is huddling low in the bushes, out of the wind.

variants.title: Junco bedtime, low and cozy
variants.body: It's getting dark, and they're picking the thickest part of the hedge and scooting in close together.

variants.title: The juncos are tucking into the hedge on {street}
variants.body: A little flock scooting low into the bushes as it gets dark, out of the wind, close together.

variants.title: The juncos are asleep low in the hedge
variants.body: Tucked close to the ground tonight, out of the wind, saving every bit of warmth for tomorrow.

variants.title: Little gray puffballs, fast asleep
variants.body: Somewhere under a hedge {place}, a few juncos are snoozing close together in the dark.

variants.title: The juncos are asleep under the hedge
variants.body: Somewhere along {street}, a few little gray puffballs are snoozing close to the ground until morning.

variants.title: The crows are commuting home
variants.body: Long lines of them crossing the evening sky, all heading to the same few roosts to sleep together.

variants.title: Crow rush hour, overhead
variants.body: Caw, caw, caw. As the light goes, everyone's heading to the big sleepover at once.

variants.title: The crows are commuting home over {street}
variants.body: Long, loose lines of them in the dusk, cawing to each other, all headed to the same big roost.

variants.title: The crows are heading to work
variants.body: Thousands slept together last night. Now, in the early light, each family is flying back to their own patch, maybe {place}.

variants.title: Crow families are fanning out for the day
variants.body: One big roost, many little neighborhoods. This morning everybody knows their route.

variants.title: The crows are heading back to their neighborhoods
variants.body: After a night in the big roost, each family is flying home to their own patch. One of those families lives around {green}, and they're landing on their usual rooftop right now.

variants.title: A crow is keeping an eye on things
variants.body: Up on the roof edge in the middle of the day, head tilting at everyone who passes. Crows remember faces. They're learning yours.

variants.title: The neighborhood watch is on duty
variants.body: A crow on the roof edge is noting who's who {place} today. They really do remember people.

variants.title: A crow is keeping an eye on {street}
variants.body: Perched on {landmark}, watching who comes and goes. Be kind: they'll remember that too.

variants.title: Crow big siblings are on babysitting duty
variants.body: Right now last year's kids are helping out, bringing food up the tree to the nest for their new little brothers and sisters.

variants.title: A crow family is feeding the new chicks
variants.body: It takes a village. Or at least a few older siblings with snacks, taking turns all day.

variants.title: A crow family is raising the new chicks together
variants.body: In a tall tree near {green}, the big kids are hopping back and forth with food. The chicks are yelling for more.

variants.title: Young crows are begging loudly
variants.body: First thing this morning: fluffy, noisy and following the parents everywhere. Patience is not a crow-kid skill.

variants.title: Crow kid, very sure they're starving
variants.body: They aren't. But they'd like everyone {place} to know they could eat breakfast right now.

variants.title: Young crows are begging loudly near {green}
variants.body: Fluffy, noisy and following their parents across the grass in the early light, absolutely convinced they're starving. They aren't.

variants.title: The crows are at a giant sleepover
variants.body: Hundreds, maybe thousands, packed into the same stand of trees tonight. Safety in numbers.

variants.title: Crow roost, lights out
variants.body: A whole city of crows, sleeping shoulder to shoulder in the dark trees, still muttering a little.

variants.title: The crows are sleeping together tonight
variants.body: Packed into one stand of trees. Somewhere in there is the family from around {green}. At first light they'll head home.

variants.title: A White-throated Sparrow is whistling
variants.body: Oh sweet Canada, Canada, Canada, thin and clear from the bushes {place} in the early light.

variants.title: Someone in the bushes is singing about Canada
variants.body: That's a White-throated Sparrow, first thing this morning. Very homesick song, very pretty.

variants.title: A White-throated Sparrow is singing about Canada
variants.body: A clear morning whistle from the bushes near {green}: oh sweet Canada, Canada, Canada.

variants.title: White-throated Sparrows are doing the leaf kick
variants.body: Both feet at once, hop-kick backward, in the middle of the day. Under every leaf, maybe a seed.

variants.title: The White-throated Sparrows are doing their hop-kick dance
variants.body: A whole little group in the leaf litter right now, kicking and checking, kicking and checking.

variants.title: White-throated Sparrows are doing the leaf kick near {green}
variants.body: Hop-kick, look, hop-kick, look, uncovering seeds one little kick at a time.

variants.title: The White-throated Sparrows are back
variants.body: They flew in from Canadian forests overnight, and this morning they're already in the bushes, whistling.

variants.title: The White-throated Sparrows are back for the winter
variants.body: First light, and the bushes around {green} are full of new neighbors from the north. Listen for their whistle.

variants.title: New neighbors in the bushes
variants.body: White-throated Sparrows just moved in for the season, hopping under the hedges all day.

variants.title: White-throated Sparrows are fueling up
variants.body: In a few weeks they'll head north. Today it's all snacks and practice songs under the bushes.

variants.title: Snack break before the big trip
variants.body: The White-throated Sparrows are eating everything they can find right now. Canada's far.

variants.title: White-throated Sparrows are fueling up near {green}
variants.body: Snacking under the bushes and practicing their song in the middle of the day.

variants.title: Chimney swifts are zipping overhead
variants.body: Out at first light, tiny cigar-shaped birds twittering and catching breakfast bugs on the wing. They hardly ever land.

variants.title: Flying cigars, twittering
variants.body: Those little zoomy birds overhead right now are chimney swifts. They eat, drink and bathe without landing.

variants.title: Chimney swifts are zipping over {street}
variants.body: Twittering, swooping, snapping up bugs above the busy block in the middle of the day.

variants.title: The swifts are pouring into a chimney
variants.body: As the light goes, they're swirling down into an old chimney {place} to sleep, clinging to the inside wall.

variants.title: Swift tornado, right on schedule
variants.body: Round and round as it gets dark, then whoosh, they all drop into the chimney for the night.

variants.title: The swifts are pouring into an old chimney
variants.body: Swirling together above {street} in the dusk, then funneling down all at once.

variants.title: The chimney swifts are back
variants.body: Fresh in from South America, and this evening there's high twittering over the rooftops again.

variants.title: Twitter, twitter, the swifts have landed
variants.body: Well, not landed. They barely ever land. But they're back, zipping overhead as the light goes.

variants.title: The chimney swifts are back over {street}
variants.body: After a very long trip, they're twittering over the rooftops tonight like they never left. Summer is on its way.

variants.title: A goose family is out for a walk
variants.body: First thing this morning: mom in front, dad at the back, and a line of fuzzy yellow goslings in between. Nobody is allowed to cut in.

variants.title: A goose family is parading toward {water}
variants.body: Two grown-ups and a wobbly line of goslings crossing the dewy grass near {green} like they own it. In a way, they do.

variants.title: The goslings are learning to graze
variants.body: Tiny beaks, very serious faces, one blade of grass at a time. A parent stands guard with a stare that says keep walking.

variants.title: The geese are grounded for a few weeks
variants.body: Their flight feathers are growing back right now, so it's floating, grazing and laying low until they can fly again.

variants.title: Geese are taking a summer break from flying
variants.body: No feathers, no flights. Today they're sticking close to the water, where a quick paddle away keeps them safe.

variants.title: The geese are spending the summer by {water}
variants.body: Floating near the edge in the middle of the day, nibbling and keeping a low profile while their new feathers grow in.

variants.title: A V of geese is honking overhead
variants.body: Heading out in the early light, taking turns at the front where the flying is hardest. The honking keeps the line together.

variants.title: A honking V is passing over {green}
variants.body: High and loud this morning, a flock crossing the sky above the neighborhood, talking the whole way.

variants.title: Geese are flying in formation
variants.body: That big wobbly V in the evening sky is a flock on the move, chatting the whole way. Listen before you look.

variants.title: A goose is standing on one foot
variants.body: The other foot is tucked up in their warm belly feathers. When this one gets cold, they'll switch.

variants.title: The geese are wintering by {water}
variants.body: Resting at the edge in the middle of the day, heads tucked and one foot up, waiting out the cold together.

variants.title: Geese are lined up along the frozen edge
variants.body: As the light goes: feathers fluffed, heads tucked, one foot up. Stay together, stay still, stay warm.

variants.title: A mallard mom has a line of ducklings
variants.body: Paddle, paddle, peep, first thing this morning. They follow her everywhere, and she keeps a very close count.

variants.title: A mallard mom is leading her ducklings around {water}
variants.body: Single file in the early light, a little fluffy parade past the reeds. She's showing them every good breakfast spot.

variants.title: Ducklings are speed-paddling to keep up
variants.body: Tiny feet going like crazy, mom gliding along like it's nothing. Every so often one zooms off and zooms right back.

variants.title: A mallard is doing a perfect handstand
variants.body: Head underwater, tail straight up, feet paddling the air, right now in the middle of the pond. The good plants are at the bottom.

variants.title: Bottoms up at the pond
variants.body: A row of duck tails pointing at the sky. The snacks are down there somewhere.

variants.title: The mallards are dabbling at {water}
variants.body: Tip forward, tail up, nibble, pop back up, over and over in the middle of the day. Very pleased with themselves.

variants.title: Two mallards are paddling side by side
variants.body: He's in his shiny green head, she's in her cozy brown, cruising the pond together in the middle of the day. They'll stay paired all winter.

variants.title: The mallard with the green head is showing off
variants.body: Head bob, tail flick, a little whistle, right now. Courting season on the pond has begun.

variants.title: Mallard couples are floating on {water}
variants.body: Two by two in the evening light, paddling slowly together toward their sleeping spot.

variants.title: The mallards are asleep at the water's edge
variants.body: Heads tucked over their backs tonight, bills under a wing, tucked in among the reeds.

variants.title: Mallards are napping in the reeds
variants.body: A few sleeping with one eye open, just in case. Very relaxing, very alert.

variants.title: The ducks are sleeping by {water}
variants.body: Tucked into the reeds in the dark, heads turned back, bills under their wings. A soft quack now and then.

variants.title: The brant just flew in from the Arctic
variants.body: Thousands of miles, and this morning here they are for the winter. Listen for their low, rolling cronk.

variants.title: The brant have landed by {water}
variants.body: Fresh in from the Arctic at first light, a flock is grazing along the shore. They'll stay till spring.

variants.title: Small dark geese are back on the shore
variants.body: Brant are here! Summer on the Arctic tundra, winter right here, and today they're settling in.

variants.title: A flock of brant is grazing the lawn
variants.body: Little dark geese with white necklaces, chatting away and nibbling grass by the water in the middle of the day.

variants.title: The brant are munching sea lettuce
variants.body: Low tide right now, and their favorite winter snack is right along the rocks. Crunchy, salty, perfect.

variants.title: Brant are grazing near {green}
variants.body: A chatty flock working across the grass one nibble at a time, little white necklaces bobbing.

variants.title: The brant are fueling up for the Arctic
variants.body: Eating as much as they can today. Soon they'll fly thousands of miles north.

variants.title: Brant are getting restless
variants.body: More chatter, more flying around in the middle of the day. Any day now they'll head for the Arctic.

variants.title: The brant are saying goodbye to {water}
variants.body: A noisy flock bobbing near the shore in the evening light, getting ready for the long flight north.

variants.title: A cormorant is drying their wings
variants.body: Up on a post in the early light, wings held wide like a little cape. Their feathers soak up water, so after the morning swim, they air-dry.

variants.title: A cormorant is striking a pose
variants.body: Wings out, chin up, very dramatic. It isn't showing off. It's laundry day.

variants.title: A cormorant is drying off on a post in {water}
variants.body: Wings spread wide, perfectly still, after a long swim chasing fish.

variants.title: A cormorant just disappeared underwater
variants.body: Swimming after fish with their feet right now, sometimes for half a minute. Watch where they pop back up.

variants.title: Cormorant on a fishing trip
variants.body: Dive, chase, gulp, in the middle of the day. They swallow fish headfirst, right at the surface.

variants.title: A cormorant is fishing in {water}
variants.body: Bob, dive, gone. Somewhere under the surface, a cormorant is chasing a snack.

variants.title: A line of cormorants is flying south
variants.body: Low over the water in the early light, a long, loose line. Winter plans: somewhere warmer.

variants.title: Cormorants are heading out
variants.body: A string of dark birds skimming the evening water, wingbeats steady, on their way south.

variants.title: Cormorants are flying low over {water}
variants.body: A long line of dark birds this morning, heading south for the winter.

variants.title: Ring-billed gulls have taken over the field
variants.body: Dozens of them in the middle of the day, standing around facing into the wind. Very organized, for gulls.

variants.title: A ring-billed gull is checking the picnic area
variants.body: Not begging. Just... supervising. Very closely. Right now.

variants.title: Ring-billed gulls are lounging near {green}
variants.body: A whole crowd of neat gray-and-white gulls on the grass, all facing the same way into the breeze, chatting.

variants.title: A ring-billed gull is patrolling the shore
variants.body: First thing this morning, walking the waterline, checking what the tide brought in overnight.

variants.title: Ring-billed gulls are walking the edge of {water}
variants.body: Up and down the waterline in the early light, peeking at everything the tide left behind.

variants.title: Gull squabble on the beach
variants.body: Two ring-bills, one snack, lots of opinions as the light goes. The snack wins.

variants.title: The ring-billed gulls are sleeping on the water
variants.body: Rafts of them tonight, floating together out where it's safe. Even gulls need a quiet night.

variants.title: A floating gull slumber party
variants.body: Hundreds of gulls bobbing on the dark water, heads tucked in.

variants.title: The gulls are asleep out on {water}
variants.body: Floating together far from shore, tucked in and quiet for once.

variants.title: A tern is diving for breakfast
variants.body: Hover, hover, SPLASH, in the early light. They plunge headfirst after tiny fish and pop right back up.

variants.title: A tern is hovering in place
variants.body: Wings flicking, eyes locked on the water. Any second now...

variants.title: A tern is diving into {water}
variants.body: Hovering high, then straight down headfirst. A tiny splash, and up they come with a silver fish.

variants.title: A tern is bringing a fish as a gift
variants.body: He's flying around showing it off right now, then he'll offer it to her. Romance, tern style.

variants.title: Tern courtship is in the air
variants.body: A fish in his beak, a little parade flight in the middle of the day. She's considering it.

variants.title: A tern is courting over {water}
variants.body: He swoops past with a fish in his beak, hoping she'll accept it.

variants.title: Tern parents are on a nonstop fish run
variants.body: Dive, catch, fly to the chicks, repeat, all day long.

variants.title: Fluffy tern chicks are waiting on the beach
variants.body: Mom and dad keep the fish coming. Everyone else should keep their distance.

variants.title: Tern parents are fishing off {water} at the end of the day
variants.body: Back and forth to the chicks one tiny fish at a time, as the light goes gold.

variants.title: The terns are heading to South America
variants.body: Today some are already flying south. A long trip for a slim little seabird. They'll be back next spring.

variants.title: Last call for the terns
variants.body: A few are still diving off the shore right now before the big flight south.

variants.title: The last terns are leaving {water}
variants.body: One more dive, then off to South America for the winter.

variants.title: A great blue heron is standing perfectly still
variants.body: Not a statue. A very patient fisher in the early light. Watch long enough and... strike!

variants.title: A great blue heron is fishing at {water}
variants.body: Knee-deep in the cold morning shallows, still as a fence post, waiting for breakfast to swim by.

variants.title: A heron is fishing in slow motion
variants.body: One step. Pause. One step. Then a lightning-fast stab.

variants.title: A great blue heron is flying home
variants.body: Huge wings, slow beats against the evening sky, neck folded into an S, legs trailing. Like a tiny dinosaur.

variants.title: Big gray bird, slow wingbeats
variants.body: That's a heron heading to roost as the light goes. Graceful, a little prehistoric.

variants.title: A heron is flapping slowly over {water}
variants.body: Neck tucked, legs trailing, heading home for the night.

variants.title: A heron is hunched by open water
variants.body: Neck pulled in, feathers fluffed, fishing in the middle of a cold day. Winter fishing takes patience.

variants.title: A heron stayed for winter
variants.body: Not all herons fly south. This one is out by the open water right now, waiting.

variants.title: A heron is waiting out the cold by {water}
variants.body: Hunched and fluffed up at the water's edge, still fishing.

variants.title: The night herons are clocking in
variants.body: Everyone else is heading to bed, and they're waking up, stretching, and stepping into the reeds to fish.

variants.title: A night heron just woke up
variants.body: Red eyes open, a big stretch, and off to work. Their shift starts right about now.

variants.title: Night herons are heading out to {water}
variants.body: As the light fades, they're leaving their daytime trees and settling in at the water's edge.

variants.title: A night heron is fishing in the dark
variants.body: Hunched and still on the shore tonight, red eyes watching the water. Very spooky, very cute.

variants.title: Night shift at the water's edge
variants.body: A stocky little heron with a black cap is waiting in the dark for something to swim by.

variants.title: A night heron is fishing along {water}
variants.body: Under the moon, waiting patiently at the edge.

variants.title: Night herons are napping in the trees
variants.body: Dozing on branches over the water in the middle of the day, hunched up like little gray loaves.

variants.title: Shh, the night herons are sleeping
variants.body: They worked all night. Right now, let them nap.

variants.title: Night herons are dozing in the trees near {water}
variants.body: A row of hunched little herons on a branch, catching up on sleep while the day goes by.

variants.title: Buffleheads are playing hide and seek
variants.body: Dive, vanish, pop up somewhere else, first thing this morning. Tiny ducks with a lot of energy.

variants.title: A bufflehead is bobbing like a bath toy
variants.body: Little black-and-white duck, big white head patch, back underwater in three, two, one.

variants.title: Buffleheads are diving out on {water}
variants.body: A little flock keeps vanishing and popping back up, white head patches flashing.

variants.title: The buffleheads are back for the winter
variants.body: Tiny diving ducks, fresh in from the forests of Canada, out on the water right now.

variants.title: Winter ducks have arrived
variants.body: Little black-and-white buffleheads are back on the water, diving like they never left.

variants.title: Buffleheads have arrived on {water}
variants.body: Fresh from northern forests, already diving. They'll be here all winter.

variants.title: The buffleheads are tucking in on the water
variants.body: A small raft floating together as the light goes, heads tucked back for the night.

variants.title: Buffleheads are drifting off to sleep
variants.body: Bobbing in a little group tonight, close together, out on the dark water.

variants.title: Buffleheads are resting on {water}
variants.body: Floating together in a tight little raft until morning.

variants.title: A swan is gliding across the pond
variants.body: Neck in a perfect S in the early light, barely a ripple. Under the water, the feet are working hard.

variants.title: A swan is preening very carefully
variants.body: Every feather, one at a time, in the middle of the day. Looking that elegant takes work.

variants.title: A mute swan is gliding on {water}
variants.body: Slow and graceful, neck curved, leaving a long soft wake behind.

variants.title: A swan is sitting on a giant nest
variants.body: A huge pile of reeds at the water's edge, and a swan on top in the middle of the day. Their partner patrols nearby. Give them lots of room.

variants.title: Swan on guard duty
variants.body: Wings slightly raised, watching everyone right now. They're protecting their eggs.

variants.title: A swan is guarding a nest by {water}
variants.body: A big mound of reeds at the edge, and a very watchful swan on top.

variants.title: Swan cygnets are riding on a parent's back
variants.body: Fluffy and gray, tucked between the wings, cruising across the pond in style in the middle of the day.

variants.title: A swan family is paddling on {water}
variants.body: Fluffy gray cygnets following their parents in a little line.

variants.title: A swan family is out for an evening paddle
variants.body: Two big white parents and a row of fuzzy gray cygnets, heading for the reeds as the light goes.

variants.title: Whoosh, whoosh, a swan is flying past
variants.body: Their wings make a loud, rhythmic hum. Right now you can hear them before you see them.

variants.title: A mute swan is taking off
variants.body: A long running start across the water, then big, loud, whooshing wings, low over the treetops.

variants.title: A swan is flying low over {water}
variants.body: Listen for the whoosh of those big wings.

variants.title: A red-winged blackbird is shouting conk-la-ree
variants.body: The sun is barely up and he's already on top of a cattail, shoulders puffed, red patches flashing. Spring is officially here.

variants.title: Conk-la-ree! from the cattails
variants.body: A male is singing his heart out in the middle of the day, showing off his red shoulders to the whole marsh.

variants.title: A red-winged blackbird is singing by {water}
variants.body: Perched on a cattail, red shoulders flashing, telling everyone nearby that this patch of reeds is taken.

variants.title: The red-winged blackbirds are back
variants.body: Among the very first birds of spring, and this morning they're claiming the best cattails.

variants.title: First sign of spring: conk-la-ree
variants.body: The blackbirds are back and very loud about it, first thing this morning.

variants.title: Red-winged blackbirds just arrived at {water}
variants.body: Early light, early spring, and they're already staking out their reeds.

variants.title: A cloud of blackbirds is swirling overhead
variants.body: Hundreds flying together in the middle of the day, gathering up before heading south.

variants.title: Blackbird flocks are gathering
variants.body: Red-wings, grackles and starlings mixing together in big, noisy flocks right now.

variants.title: Blackbirds are swirling over {green}
variants.body: A big noisy flock in the evening sky, gathering before the trip south.

variants.title: A deer is stepping out of the trees
variants.body: First light, ears forward, nose working, one slow step at a time onto the dewy grass.

variants.title: A deer is grazing at the edge of {green}
variants.body: Quiet and careful in the early light, just inside the trees, ears turning toward every sound.

variants.title: A deer is nibbling at the edge of the woods
variants.body: As the light goes, big ears turning like satellite dishes, listening to everything.

variants.title: A spotted fawn is hiding in the tall grass
variants.body: Mom is grazing nearby this morning. The fawn is staying perfectly still. If you see one, smile and walk away.

variants.title: A deer mom and her fawn are out together
variants.body: The fawn wobbling after her on very long legs, white spots and all.

variants.title: A deer mom is feeding near {green}
variants.body: As the light goes, her spotted fawn is tucked in the tall grass nearby, waiting perfectly still.

variants.title: A deer just flipped up their white tail
variants.body: Something startled them this morning. That white flag says: I'm out of here. Bound, bound, gone.

variants.title: White tails bouncing into the woods
variants.body: A little group of deer, startled in the dusk, bounding away with tails up.

variants.title: A deer is bounding back into the trees near {green}
variants.body: White tail up like a flag in the early light, three big leaps, and gone.

variants.title: A deer is munching acorns
variants.body: Fall is snack season, and right now everyone is bulking up for winter under the oaks.

variants.title: A buck with new antlers is out
variants.body: He's careful and quiet in the middle of the day, nibbling acorns.

variants.title: Deer are eating acorns near {green}
variants.body: As the light goes, a few deer are making the most of the oaks.

variants.title: A mockingbird is singing a medley
variants.body: A robin, a cardinal, a car alarm, a squeaky gate, all before breakfast. Each song twice, then the next.

variants.title: The neighborhood DJ is on
variants.body: Twenty different songs and counting, from the top of an antenna. No two minutes sound the same.

variants.title: A mockingbird is performing above {street}
variants.body: From the highest antenna around, running through every song they've ever heard, including a few car alarms.

variants.title: A mockingbird is singing in the middle of the night
variants.body: An unpaired male, still going under the city lights. Very romantic. Very loud.

variants.title: Someone's singing under the streetlight
variants.body: That's a mockingbird, still going at midnight, hoping someone special is listening.

variants.title: A mockingbird is serenading {street} at midnight
variants.body: Under the streetlights, a lonely male singing song after song.

variants.title: A mockingbird is guarding a berry bush
variants.body: This bush is theirs for the winter, and right now a robin is getting chased off.

variants.title: Mockingbird flashing their wings
variants.body: Lifting their wings to show white patches. Maybe to startle bugs, maybe just to show off.

variants.title: A mockingbird is defending a berry bush near {green}
variants.body: All day long, this one bush is theirs.

variants.title: A cardinal is feeding his partner
variants.body: First thing this morning he hops over with a seed and passes it to her beak to beak. It's basically a kiss.

variants.title: A cardinal couple is sharing snacks near {green}
variants.body: In the early light he picks a seed and hands it over, right there in the hedge.

variants.title: Cardinal couple goals
variants.body: He's bringing her snacks all day, and she's singing back from the hedge. They're together all year.

variants.title: A red cardinal is glowing in the hedge
variants.body: Bright red against the gray morning, puffed up round, checking for breakfast seeds.

variants.title: A cardinal is visiting the hedges along {street}
variants.body: A flash of red in the bare branches at first light, round and puffed up against the cold.

variants.title: A cardinal is fluffed up like a red tomato
variants.body: Feathers puffed out to stay warm in the middle of a cold day. Very round, very red.

variants.title: A cardinal is whistling cheer, cheer, cheer
variants.body: Loud and clear from the top of a tree in the early light. Listen: the female might sing back.

variants.title: Birdie, birdie, birdie
variants.body: That's a cardinal, whistling from the treetop at first light.

variants.title: A cardinal is whistling over {street}
variants.body: Cheer, cheer, cheer, loud and bright, as the neighborhood wakes up.

variants.title: The cardinals are the last ones at the snack bar
variants.body: As the light fades, they're still in the hedge, grabbing one more seed.

variants.title: A cardinal is calling chip, chip in the dusk
variants.body: One last check-in with their partner before bed.

variants.title: Cardinals are grabbing a late snack near {green}
variants.body: The last birds out tonight, picking at seeds in the bushes as it gets dark.

variants.title: A grackle is strutting across the lawn
